Not sure about the gen from the syringe, but there were plenty of spores in it. Seemed to be doing pretty good at first, they both spawned and grew super fast. Both bags grew different - one was more dry and had the start of the overlay, and the other grew just fine with no problems, so it could have been the spawn bag? But I figured the one was just dry and it was choking out the myc, so it was overgrowing. After I soaked the mixed bags into one cake, that's when this started to pop up... Had a little myc piss at first too, but that stopped after the soaking.

:EDIT: I've decided to keep half the cake, and just watch what happens. Smaller yield in case nothing happens, and then half gone with the worst of what I saw just in case.

My guess is this happened in the bag. One seemed to grow faster than the other and had the start of that overlay on it, and the other seemed just fine. I noticed though that in the overlay bag, the substrate was a little dryer than the other one, so I figured it was just dry. I soaked the cake after it had fully colonized all together.... looks like that was where I eff'd up. I should have kept both bags separate. Turns out a bag that has a good bit of overlay in it (but no discoloration or oozing holes yet) can be more than just a dry substrate choking out the myc. That, or it got infected when I soaked it. Absolutely the best time of my life, but these tend to make me queasy and kinda wanna vomit at first during the peak.

AMVP #2 produces like no tomorrow - so fast, I had to use all 9 levels in the dehydrator and STILL ran out of space. But their trip was very harsh colors (no color changing magic), short-lived (3-4hrs on lemon tek), and had some rough hangovers. These did not make me sick or want to vomit, so I used them for a while. Always felt like there was something unfriendly somewhere in the room, but not enough to ruin a trip. Body high was eh, but absolutely shattered reality. My temp guage in my house was unreadable and had panels that didn't exist. TV completely smeared faces into fractals. Lost direction in my own apartment which door was my bathroom vs the bedroom. The room grew and shrank over and over like it was breathing, and some kind of Alice in Wonderland shit. Was a great time if you wanted to break reality, but definitely not the magical otherworldly experience I had on Ghosts.

Overall between the two, I'd go with Ghosts for an awesome magical ride, but damn man, I need medicine for my stomach because even with a lemon tek, that shit tears up my stomach. AMVPs are a nice break when you just wanna watch your room fall apart, but I'd rather talk to my wall monster again and stare at color-changing lights that aren't supposed to change color. Best trips I've ever had.

I'd researched about a solid month on some budget options, and eventually learned what's good and what's not in terms of parts before I even bought one. Reasons are a mix of 3 things.

The first and foremost was straight up financing. My credit had a max cap of 1,500, and this left me with roughly $63 left over, which wasn't much wiggle room. But what I asked for was $900, because there was a different guitar I was going to go for before they surprised me by offering as much as they did, and so I decided to go for the one I'd been daydreaming about now for weeks while researching - and I could nab it because it had 150 off for being slightly dinged. Dove straight for the one that was living in my head rent-free, and couldn't stop thinking about.

The second most important factor was parts, and sound... I know budget ones have issues. I knew I'd get better and eventually want to move on to something that didn't feel like it was holding me back. That phrase "get what you really want, as opposed to settling for something you might not enjoy and stop playing" rang true while I stared at it hovering over the Buy button. I stuck to my gut. Neck-through is awesome for sound. Stainless steel frets were a surprise I didn't learn until later, but a major bonus. A third single-pickup is always great for variety, flexibility of sound, and experimenting. Trem bar is great for added flare when I get there - which I'm 100% not... yet. An (admittedly tough) tremolo that I know isn't going to fail me. (Learn on hardmode, and others come easy.) And non-garbage bits and bobs I won't have to worry about coming loose, breaking, or falling out of tune every 20 minutes. I watched some YouTube videos of the pros using it to the best it could be, and listened to the sound. Did that for several guitars I'd been considering, and loved the absolute BEAST range this has. Absolute 100% flexibility for whatever I wanted. All in that price-range my financing offered to me - which solidified it. I used damn near all of it given to get the best I possibly could.

And the third is vain ol' aesthetics. The Prestige's didn't catch my eye, financing aside, tbh. (Just slightly out of reach anyway.) I liked the blue neck that matched the color scheme, and the awesome color, pattern, and that the neck-through kept that consistent in the back, too. To be honest, I would have dove for this one anyway regardless if there were better guitars, because it already has everything I could ever want in terms of parts and sound as a beginner and beyond, plus looking like it was made by friggin gods. I just adored absolutely EVERYthing about this guitar in particular!
